question.text: The BEP for a bear call spread with strikes 83/83.50 and net premium 0.06 is:

answer.text: 83.06 (same as bull call spread with same strikes)

explanation.text: The Logic: BEP = Lower strike + Net premium = 83 + 0.06 = 83.06. The workbook's bear call spread example on pp.105-106 and bull call spread example on p.103 both use the same strikes and net premium and produce the same BEP of 83.06. The Trap: Both bull and bear call spreads with the same strikes and premiums have the SAME BEP, even though their directional profiles are opposite. Note: Below 83.06 the bear call spread profits and the bull call spread loses; above 83.06 the positions reverse. Source: NISM-Series-I Currency Derivatives workbook, p.103 and pp.105-106.
